text: Shift books back sixty years, one to a spine, in date order.
The last four are thinner than the ones before them.
The very last one has three months in it and then stops.
The sample bench. Chippings in trays, labelled by face and by depth.
Half the trays have a second label stuck over the first, printed:
MERIDIAN FOUNDATION - COLLECTED. And a date this spring.
The weighbridge counter, and the great brass wheel of the scale
coming up through the floor behind it.
It reads zero. It has read zero for two years.
Two dial gauges plumbed into the rock, watching the west face.
One of them has not moved since it was fitted.
The other one moves. Not much. Not steadily. But it moves.
A shelf of things brought up out of the workings and never claimed:
a boot, a tin whistle, a child's slate with sums on it,
and a lamp that somebody in this office still fills every Friday.
